Victoria Plaisir

October 6, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Manager:

I am excited to apply for the Outreach Manager – Behavioral Health position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With more than six years of experience supporting youth, families, and community-based programs, I have developed a strong background in community outreach, relationship building, participant engagement, resource navigation, and coordinated service delivery. I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines relationship development with helping individuals and families connect to services that can meaningfully improve their lives.

In my current role as a Success Coach with Hispanic Unity of Florida, I manage a caseload of more than 25 youth and families and work directly with participants to identify needs, develop individualized service plans, coordinate referrals, and connect families with appropriate community resources. I regularly collaborate with interdisciplinary teams and community partners to address barriers affecting participant progress. I also coordinate family engagement workshops and support events designed to strengthen participation and community relationships. This experience has strengthened my ability to build trust, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, identify needs, and follow through to ensure individuals are connected with the appropriate resources.

Previously, as a Program Specialist with Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami, I worked extensively with youth, families, volunteers, schools, and community partners. I supported more than 75 youth and volunteer mentoring matches and conducted outreach initiatives focused on recruiting and engaging participants. I also collaborated with schools and community organizations to address barriers affecting student success. Through this work, I developed a strong understanding of how effective outreach depends on consistent relationship management, clear communication, and the ability to understand the needs of both the individuals being served and the organizations serving them.

I also bring strong experience with program documentation, data tracking, and CRM systems. At Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami, I used Salesforce to document services, track participant outcomes, maintain records, and support reporting. In my current position, I maintain accurate participant documentation and ensure services and referrals are properly coordinated and documented. I understand that successful outreach is not simply about making connections; it also requires organized follow-through, measurable activity, and strong communication with internal teams. These skills would allow me to effectively coordinate with Admissions, maintain outreach activity within a CRM, and support timely connections to care.

My earlier experience at Riverside House further strengthened my ability to work with individuals experiencing complex circumstances. I conducted daily intakes, coordinated services for more than 30 clients, monitored program compliance, maintained confidential records, and responded to crises using de-escalation techniques and established emergency protocols. This experience taught me the importance of professionalism, discretion, empathy, and sound judgment when working with individuals and families who may be navigating significant challenges.

I am especially drawn to the opportunity to represent both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center within the community. The ability to educate schools, healthcare professionals, therapists, treatment providers, and community organizations about available programs while helping facilitate connections to appropriate care is work I find meaningful. I would bring a relationship-driven, organized, and service-oriented approach to developing referral partnerships and expanding awareness of behavioral health resources throughout the community.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth services, community outreach, participant engagement, resource coordination, and program operations can contribute to the continued growth of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Victoria Plaisir

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English. As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID.

Dear Hiring Manager,

When I saw that Adolescent Wellness Academy was hiring for a bilingual Adolescent Mental Health Program Coordinator, I knew I had to apply. As a bilingual advocate fluent in English and Spanish, I regularly orient Spanish-speaking families through institutional processes, translate complex paperwork, and deliver culturally sensitive communication to ensure families feel welcomed and supported from their first interaction with care.

My passion is helping individuals and families identify their needs, connecting them to vital resources, and creating structured, empowering environments for youth. I thrive in collaborative settings where detailed organization, clear communication, and empathetic support intersect to improve client care.

I would love the opportunity to contribute my skills and dedication to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s virtual PHP and IOP programs. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to learning more about the Adolescent Mental Health Program Coordinator position.

Thank you for your time and consideration,
Pam Collins

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a behavioral health leadership, clinical operations, or clinical management opportunity within your organization. With a PhD in Psychology, Master’s-level training in Psychology, MCAP/CAP credentials, and extensive experience in behavioral health, substance use treatment, clinical supervision, and program operations, I bring a combination of clinical knowledge, leadership experience, and operational expertise that allows me to effectively support both clients and multidisciplinary teams.

I currently serve as a Clinical Director with Recovery Unplugged, where I provide clinical leadership within a substance use and co-occurring mental health treatment environment serving clients across residential and outpatient levels of care. My responsibilities include supporting clinical programming, supervising and collaborating with treatment professionals, reviewing clinical documentation, monitoring treatment progress, addressing client needs, facilitating therapeutic programming, and helping maintain quality and continuity of care. My experience with clinical systems and documentation platforms, including KIPU and other behavioral health technologies, has strengthened my ability to manage clinical operations while maintaining attention to compliance, documentation, and patient-centered care.

Prior to my current role, I developed significant leadership experience within behavioral health and correctional settings, including supervisory responsibilities across multiple facilities and teams. Throughout my career, I have been entrusted with increasing levels of responsibility, progressing from direct-service substance abuse counseling into supervisory and leadership positions. I have experience conducting clinical and operational reviews, supporting staff development, coordinating services, addressing complex client needs, and maintaining program standards. My background has also required me to work effectively with individuals experiencing substance use disorders, mental health concerns, trauma-related challenges, and complex psychosocial circumstances.

My academic and professional background has provided me with a strong foundation in evidence-based behavioral health practices, clinical assessment, treatment planning, group facilitation, and organizational leadership. I approach leadership with a balance of accountability and compassion, recognizing that successful clinical programs depend not only on quality services for clients but also on strong communication, effective supervision, teamwork, and a culture that supports professional growth.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to behavioral health to your organization. I am confident that my combination of direct clinical experience and executive-level operational perspective would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your team and the individuals you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications can support your organization’s goals.

Sincerely,

Dr. Richild Morgan, PhD, MCAP
Behavioral Health Executive | Clinical Director | Clinical Operations Leader
Fort Lauderdale–Miami, Florida

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Program Operations Manager position with Adolescent Behavioral Health. With a background in forensic psychology and healthcare operations, combined with several years of experience leading teams, developing workflows, and supporting patients and healthcare partners, I am excited by the opportunity to bring my leadership and operational experience to an organization focused on improving the lives of adolescents and their families.

In my current role within a healthcare organization specializing in Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) and Chronic Care Management (CCM), I lead a team of 13 employees supporting patients, healthcare providers, and clinical partners. I oversee day-to-day operations, quality and performance, escalations, process improvement, staff coaching, and the development of workflows and standard operating procedures. I joined the organization while it was still a young startup with limited structure and had the opportunity to help build and develop the support operation as the company grew. This experience has taught me how to thrive in fast-paced environments, identify operational gaps, build practical solutions, and lead teams through change.

My academic background in forensic psychology has given me a strong foundation in behavioral science, human development, and the factors that influence behavior and decision-making. I am particularly drawn to adolescent behavioral health because of the opportunity to combine that academic foundation with my professional experience in healthcare, leadership, and operations. While I am not a clinician, I understand the importance of creating an environment where clinical teams can do their work effectively and where patients and families feel supported, respected, and cared for.

As a leader, I take a hands-on and collaborative approach. I believe in setting clear expectations, supporting employees with the resources and coaching they need to succeed, and holding people accountable while recognizing their strengths and contributions. I also enjoy building structure in evolving environments and continuously looking for ways to improve workflows, communication, and the overall experience for both staff and the individuals we serve.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare leadership experience, operational mindset, and background in forensic psychology to your team. I am particularly excited about the possibility of contributing to a growing behavioral-health program where strong operations and compassionate leadership can directly support better outcomes for adolescents and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and perspective could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Mariam Dominguez

I am very grateful for the opportunity to grow from an individual contributor into a leadership position and to develop skills that I know will continue to serve me throughout my career.  At this point, however, I am looking for an opportunity to reconnect with the area I am most passionate about: forensic psychology, community work, and helping individuals who may be facing difficult circumstances. My academic background and earlier professional experiences were centered around the forensic and legal systems, and I have always felt strongly that this is the type of work I ultimately want to return to. I would like to use the leadership and operational experience I have gained in healthcare while getting my foot back in the door within a field that is more closely aligned with my education and long-term career goals.  I am also ready to return to an in-person work environment. My current position is entirely remote, and while I have learned a great deal from that experience, I genuinely miss the collaboration, connection, and sense of purpose that comes from working alongside people in person and being directly involved in the community.  Overall, I am not looking to leave my current role because of a negative experience. questionnaire.response: I think my supervisor would say that one of my biggest areas for growth has been learning to delegate more effectively and not feeling like I need to personally take ownership of every problem.  I naturally take a very hands-on approach to my work, and when something needs to be done, my instinct is often to jump in and make sure it gets done correctly. Earlier in my leadership experience, that sometimes meant taking on more than I needed to instead of trusting my team to take ownership themselves.  As I have grown as a manager, I have learned that effective leadership is not about being the person who solves every problem. It is about developing your team, giving people ownership, and knowing when your involvement is most valuable. I have become much more intentional about delegating responsibilities, setting clear expectations, and allowing my team to work through challenges while remaining available to support them.  I still consider myself a very hands-on leader, but I have learned how to balance that with giving my team the autonomy they need to grow. I think that has been an important part of my development as a manager.

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Principles Recovery
Application for Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Manager,
Principles Recovery’s commitment to supporting individuals and families on their recovery journey deeply resonates with my professional background. With over eight years of dedicated experience in behavioral health admissions and a proven track record of turning inquiries into successful admissions, I am eager to contribute to your mission.

In my previous role as Admissions Coordinator/Business Development at ARH Medical Group, ICBD Holdings, Discovery Institute, and a few others, I orchestrated high-volume intake processes, meticulously ensuring precise data entry, documentation, and record maintenance in strict adherence to HIPAA regulations. I
successfully validated insurance coverage and secured authorizations, optimizing billing
accuracy and timely reimbursement. This experience directly aligns with your need for an individual adept at navigating complex insurance details and coordinating with utilization review and clinical teams, ensuring a seamless transition for prospective clients.

My resume highlights a strong history of exceeding goals, such as when I directed national sales strategies for diabetic supplies and associated healthcare products at Dedicated Medical Providers, demonstrating my capacity for driving results through strategic planning and persuasive communication. I am particularly skilled at guiding callers from initial contact
through admission, building trust, and addressing barriers with empathy and professionalism. This ability, combined with my proficiency in CRM systems like Salesforce and a solid understanding of various levels of care, positions me to effectively manage admissions and help Principles Recovery hit its census targets. I am also experienced in mentoring admissions staff, sharing best practices and closing strategies to foster a high-performing team environment. My background in both direct admissions coordination and broader business development has equipped me with a
comprehensive understanding of the operational and client-facing aspects essential for this role. I am confident in my ability to not only manage but enhance your admissions process.

I am enthusiastic about the opportunity to leverage my skills in admissions coordination,
insurance verification, and client advocacy to support Principles Recovery’s growth and,
more importantly, the recovery of the individuals and families you serve. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how I can contribute to your team.

Kind Regards,

Cassandra Leaman

October 13, 2026

Hiring Manager
Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Substance Use Treatment
Dear Hiring Manager,

Throughout my career in behavioral health, I have had the privilege of walking alongside individuals during some of the most difficult and vulnerable moments of their lives. I have witnessed firsthand the challenges of addiction, the courage it takes to ask for help, and the incredible difference that access to appropriate treatment can make. These experiences have not only shaped me as a professional but have strengthened my belief that everyone deserves to feel supported, understood, and hopeful when taking their first steps toward recovery. It is with this passion that I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center.

In my current role as a behavioral health counselor, I work extensively with individuals experiencing substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health challenges. My responsibilities include conducting comprehensive assessments, determining appropriate levels of care using ASAM criteria, developing individualized treatment recommendations, and helping coordinate referrals to additional treatment services. Through my work with Intensive Outpatient Programs, outpatient services, and residential treatment referrals, I have developed a strong understanding of the treatment continuum and the importance of helping individuals access care that meets their unique needs.

One of the most meaningful aspects of my work has been building connections with individuals who may feel overwhelmed, discouraged, or uncertain about seeking treatment. I understand that reaching out for help is not always easy and that the compassion, patience, and understanding someone receives during those initial interactions can make a lasting difference. I strive to approach every individual with dignity, empathy, and encouragement while helping them navigate the often-complex process of accessing behavioral health services.

In addition to my clinical experience, I bring strong organizational, communication, and care coordination skills. Managing a substantial caseload has strengthened my ability to balance competing priorities, maintain accurate documentation, communicate effectively with multidisciplinary providers, and ensure that individuals receive appropriate follow-up and support. I am comfortable working independently, navigating electronic health records, and collaborating with community partners to reduce barriers to treatment.

What excites me most about this opportunity is the ability to continue making a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals seeking recovery while focusing my professional skills on connecting people with the services they need. I believe the admissions process is much more than an administrative responsibility; it is an opportunity to offer reassurance, build trust, and help someone recognize that recovery is possible.

I would be honored to bring my experience, dedication, and genuine compassion for individuals in recovery to the admissions team at Principles Recovery Center. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and passion for helping others could contribute to your organization's mission.
Sincerely,

Cynthia “Morgan” Fazekas
